title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval - Lumina Health
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results for Lumina Health prompt sets. Discussed drop in certain clinical intent accuracy, candidate fixes (prompt tuning, few-shot examples, score thresholds), and next steps to run targeted regression tests + safety/PII guardrails. Action owners assigned for benchmark rerun, prompt updates, and security docs follow-up.
next_steps: Redwood to run regression test over expanded prompt set by 2026-09-28
Lumina to provide 50 additional edge-case prompts by 2026-09-25
Redwood SE to share updated prompt templates and scoring spreadsheet
Schedule security deep-dive with Tom (Lumina) week of 2026-10-05
action_items: Priya K. (Redwood) - Rerun eval with updated scoring thresholds and send csv of failures - due 2026-09-28
Ethan W. (Lumina) - Share 50 edge-case prompts and 10 real transcripts - due 2026-09-25
Alex C. (Redwood AE) - Send pricing/next-phase pilot options and remind about Dedicated capacity pricing - due 2026-09-24

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-23 10:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Marta Gonzales (Lumina Head of Clinical AI); Ethan Wu (Lumina ML Eng); Sara O'Neal (Lumina PM); Tom Rivera (Lumina Security)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly POC sync for Lumina. we wanted to go over the quality evals from last week's runs and talk next steps. Priya, you wanna kick off with the results?

[00:18] Priya: sure, yeah. I ran the expanded prompt set against the two models we had in pilot, the redwood verified open-3-small and the quantized variant on our dedicated runner. quick caveat: some of the transcriptions in the test harness were a bit noisy so we see a few label flips, but overall numbers are valid.

[00:35] Priya: baseline accuracy for clinical-intent classification was 92% on the control set; current run shows 87% for the production prompt set, and we saw the biggest regressions on "medication-adjustment" and "follow-up-timing" intents.

[00:52] Marta: that's the portion we're most worried about, because the UI surfaces specific care recommendations and we can't have high false positives there. can you break down examples?

[01:05] Priya: yep, I'll share the spreadsheet after. brief examples: short free-text like "patient wants to lower dosage" sometimes maps to 'schedule follow-up' instead of 'change medication' - looks like prompt context isn't anchoring the intent, and the model overweights recency.

[01:22] Ethan: is this more a model capacity issue or prompt framing? I know we tried few-shot vs zero-shot, did you see a big delta?

[01:34] Priya: few-shot improved precision by ~3 points on those intents, but also increased token usage which bumps cost and slightly increased latency. so it's a tradeoff - few-shot helps but cost/latency tradeoff for high volume matters.

[01:50] Alex: right, latency vs cost is always the tradeoff. for pilot we can do targeted few-shot for the critical intents and keep others zero-shot. Redwood can configure route-specific prompt templates so you only pay extra where it matters.

[02:06] Sara: related, how deterministic are the results? the product team cares about stability across releases. we had a regression last week after a model roll.

[02:18] Priya: good point. we did notice one regression after the quantized variant was swapped in for some sequences - likely due to tokenization edge-case with some clinical shorthand. we'll add a regression harness that runs prompt set A/B across model variants and flags >2% delta.

[02:36] Jordan: to add, we'll tie that to alerting in Console so you'll see failures per route and example inputs. You can set tolerances per intent.

[02:46] Tom: quick sec on security - can you confirm where the prompt logs live? are they in your control plane or can we keep them in our VPC? also KMS, encryption at rest, SSO?

[02:58] Alex: yes. for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys and VPC-only logs; for hosted we redact PHI by default but we should share the security pack. we'll follow up with SOC2 + KMS docs; Priya can pull the exact retention policy we used in the pilot.

[03:14] Tom: okay, we'll need the SOC2 + KMS config and info about audit logs for compliance.

[03:22] Priya: noted. back to quality - one of the low-hanging fixes is to strengthen the guardrails: explicit output constraints, answer templates, and a post-classification filter that rejects outputs with PII or ambiguous recommendations. we tested a simple regex-based filter and it caught ~60% of PII slips but missed structured shorthand.

[03:44] Ethan: can we add a small entity-recognizer pre-filter? we've got an internal NER model that flags PHI; if we pipe that before the LLM we can avoid some risky prompts.

[03:54] Priya: absolutely. Redwood can route through an external pre-filter step or you can do it client-side before sending. both are doable; we just need to decide latency tolerance.

[04:07] Alex: let's document options: 1) client-side NER pre-filter (zero cost to Redwood, minimal latency), 2) Redwood pipeline pre-filter (more integrated, needs config), 3) post-output filter in Console for monitoring.

[04:23] Marta: on scoring, what metric did you use? F1? precision heavy? for clinical we prefer precision higher than recall because false positives are worse.

[04:34] Priya: we used precision/recall/F1 and an intent-specific weighted score. for the dashboard we show per-intent precision and a composite weighted accuracy. right now threshold tuned for recall gave better coverage but lowered precision; we can flip to precision-weighted for clinical intents.

[04:51] Ethan: how about human-in-the-loop? for high-risk intents we want a reviewer flag. can Redwood send a review queue?

[05:02] Jordan: yes. we have workflow hooks to route outputs to a review queue in your system or ours; metadata includes model version, prompt id, and confidence score. small note: some of those metadata fields got truncated in earlier runs due to our anonymization step - we'll fix that.

[05:18] Priya: action items from the quality side: rerun regression with precision-first thresholds, add few-shot templates for two critical intents, and produce CSV of failure examples for your team.

[05:30] Marta: sounds good. timeline?

[05:33] Priya: we can have the regression rerun and a results csv by Monday, 2026-09-28, assuming we get the additional 50 edge-case prompts you mentioned.

[05:44] Ethan: we'll compile those by Friday, 2026-09-25.

[05:48] Tom: and security follow-up?

[05:51] Alex: I'll send the security packet today and schedule a deeper meeting for the week of Oct 5th for Tom and our security SME.

[06:01] Sara: one other note - we saw some hallucination cases where the model invented follow-up times not in the note. is there a quick guardrail?

[06:10] Priya: yes, template enforcement plus a fidelity check that compares entity mentions in prompt vs output helps; also adding a rejection condition if output includes dates/times not present in input. we'll include that in the updated prompt templates.

[06:26] Alex: pricing note - if you want Dedicated to keep all logs in your VPC with KMS, that's a different SKU. I'll follow up with numbers.

[06:36] Marta: understood.

[06:38] Priya: anything else from Lumina?

[06:41] Marta: no, that's it. thanks, team.

[06:44] Alex: great, recap quick: Redwood to rerun regression with precision thresholds and share CSV of failures by 9/28; Lumina to send 50 edge-case prompts by 9/25; Redwood to send security packet and schedule security deep-dive week of 10/05; Alex to send pilot pricing options by 9/24.

[07:05] Jordan: I'll put the action items into the shared drive and tag owners.

[07:12] Alex: cool, thanks everyone. end call.

Notes: transcript has occasional mislabels and noise; some product names were transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cash" in the auto-export but corrected in convo above. Links shared: prompt_templates_v2.xlsx (link), quality_results_sep23.csv (link), security_packet_redwood.pdf (link).
